subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Photolithography: Printing Circuits with Light
description: A quick, practical guide to Photolithography: Printing Circuits with Light.

hook.text: To put billions of transistors on a chip, engineers print patterns with ultraviolet light.

buildup.text: A photosensitive coating is exposed through a mask. Light hardens or softens the resist.

discovery.text: Developers wash away the exposed (or unexposed) resist, leaving a precise pattern behind.

twist.text: EUV lithography uses 13.5 nm wavelength light — shorter than visible — to print 3 nm features.

climax.text: One EUV machine costs $200 million and only one company in the world makes them.

punchline.text: Printing with light at the atomic scale — that's how chips are made.

quiz.question: Why is EUV lithography needed for modern chips?
options: It uses cheaper light sources than older methods
Its shorter wavelength can print features as small as 3 nanometers
It works faster than all previous lithography techniques
